title: Louis Armstrong telling a story with one note
summary: Everybody was listening to Louis, who could swing people with a single note; Dickenson remembers his solo behind a blues singer on record.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Yes. Of course, Louis could tell a story with one note. He didn't have to have no whole lot of notes or nothin'. Just that one note would swing people.
Yeah. I guess everybody was listening to Louis then.
You told me you heard him pretty early, like on records with Blues singers and stuff.
Yeah, there was one piece that has lately been revived. I don't know who is the guy that sings it. I can't think of who it was. 'Of All The Wrongs You've Done To Me.'
I heard Louis play that years ago. He played a beautiful solo on it. You know how the singer stops and lets the guy play a little bit.
I think Bechet was on that, too, if I'm not mistaken.
Really? I don't know who was on that particular record. I know Louis played a beautiful solo on it.
That's a pretty song, too. Yes. That was before you... When did you see him live the first time?
Gee, I don't know. I don't know. I have no idea.
